body:
Merged upstream main into the contributor branch after #3205 merged. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled reference includes the upstream and Agie tools.

The PR body records the results for `d982d452b`. All 104 targeted tests and strict all-target Clippy passed. A fresh export reproduced the six controller-checked files. The 254-step heavy gate is in progress. The PR remains a draft while it runs.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d982d452be45cc8a123906b0e73311126f384020 -->
Not built - needs a maintainer look. No blocking source finding. This is not a verified build or a safety clearance.

What looks good:

- Creation uses the undoable operation command. CLI, MCP and desktop export use the same application entry point.
- Export checks the selected source, threading disk, rounded topology, arc extrema and mounted travel before publication.
- The native script deletes working steps and does not create them. The receipt identifies unverified holding, leads and erosion settings.
- The body includes before and after desktop screenshots. The partial work uses `Refs #3178` and `Refs #3179`.

Local results:

- The trial merge with upstream/main at `ced4dc34e743b75a2e6d7836c998dcc5f2c1fa79` completed without conflicts.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...review-3219` passed.
- Build, quick gate, touched suites and Clippy: not run. `crates/post/Cargo.toml:21` adds direct dependencies on `tempfile`, `rustix` and `windows-sys`. The reviewer rules require a maintainer decision before a build of this dependency change. `Cargo.lock` also changes.
- No GitHub runner or workflow was used.

Extra suites run:

- None. The dependency rule prevented test execution.
- No fixture or golden directory changes. No moved goldens require a line review.
- The diff does not change the STEP, mesh or model import code. The additional kernel import suites do not apply.

Safety verification:

- This change affects geometry and native controller output. It requires the safety tier.
- Reviewer mutations: not run because of the dependency rule. No red/green mutation result is claimed.
- The author reports 104 targeted tests, strict Clippy and 254 passing heavy steps on this head. These are author results, not reviewer results.
- After the dependency decision, local tests and at least two safety mutations remain necessary before a verified clean review.

Requested source changes: none.

Maintainer decision: inspect the dependency additions and the platform publication code in `crates/post/src/agie_setup/publish.rs`. The review label is `needs-maintainer`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Maintainer decision, 2026-11-22: the Agie stack goes one PR at a time, after #2951.

- The approvals for #2951 carry over to this PR: the direct dependencies `tempfile`, `rustix` and `windows-sys` in `crates/post`, and the Agie-CAM reference (MIT).
- This PR gets its own independent safety read and a trial-merge gate after #2951 merges.
- #2993 and #2999 stay drafts until their turn. They are refreshed then.

The label `needs-maintainer` is removed.

The recorded decision on this PR stands (comment 7080044891, "Maintainer decision, 2026-11-22: the Agie stack goes one PR at a time, after #2951"):
- The approvals for #2951 carry over to this PR: the direct dependencies `tempfile`, `rustix` and `windows-sys` in `crates/post`, and the Agie-CAM reference (MIT).
- This PR gets its own independent safety read and a trial-merge gate after #2951 merges.

No owner decision is open here. If you see a change that the decision does not cover, name it in a comment. A label with a named reason stays.

Coordinator, a rule for this PR and the PRs stacked on it (#2993, #2999 and those after them).

The maintainer reported #3537: the word "Agie" shows in text that the user reads as if it were a feature, an operation or a post type. Agie is a machine. The dialects are Klartext and ISO wire EDM. The posted output and the goldens must not change. The machine file and the model name stay.

Thus:
- This PR does not merge before the naming plan of #3537 is known, unless the text that it adds is only on the machine side (a machine file, a model name).
- When the rename of #3537 merges, we tell you here which names changed, so that this branch can take them.
- The other steps of the recorded decision (comment 7080044891) stay: an independent safety read and a trial-merge gate, one PR at a time. #2951 merged at 17:40Z, so the chain is on `main` now.

@qsmits no action is needed from you now. If you plan new user-facing text in this stack, use the machine name only where the text names the machine.

Maintainer decision (owner, live answer 2026-11-23): the new dependencies of `crates/post` are not approved at this time. The label `needs-maintainer` stays. No build and no refresh starts until the owner decides on your answer.

The PR adds three dependencies to `crates/post`: `tempfile`, `rustix` (feature `fs`) and `windows-sys` (feature `Win32_Storage_FileSystem`). Please answer these questions for each one:

1. What does the export need it for? Name the function and the failure that it prevents (for example the staged write, or the rename that does not replace an existing file).
2. Can `std` do it? For example `std::fs::File::create_new`, `std::fs::hard_link` plus `remove_file`, or a staging name in the target folder with `std::fs::rename`.
3. Can a crate that the workspace has already do it? Name the crate if you checked one.
4. If the dependency must stay: can it be a dev-dependency only, or stay behind a `cfg` for one platform?

Thank you for the work. The PR also conflicts with `main` now; that can wait until the dependency question has an answer.

Thank you for the questions. Short answer: this PR adds no new dependency to `main`. The three dependencies are on `main` already.

- `main` got them in commit `3845cb70e` (#2951, "feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job"). The approval for #2951 covered them.
- On `main`, `crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs` uses them (lines 104, 129 and 151). `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs` uses `tempfile`.
- This PR moves the same publish code into `crates/post/src/agie_setup/publish.rs`. The `Cargo.toml` diff shows the lines only because the branch base is older than #2951. After the refresh, the PR does not change `crates/post/Cargo.toml`.

Answers to the four questions, for each dependency:

**`tempfile`**
1. `publish` writes all job files into a staging folder next to the destination. Then one rename publishes the folder. This prevents a partial job on the disk if a write fails. The guard removes the staging folder on each error path.
2. Yes, in part. `std::fs::create_dir` with a unique name in the target folder can make the staging folder. The cleanup on error must then be written by hand.
3. No other crate in the workspace makes a temporary folder in production code. `crates/app` has `tempfile` as a dev-dependency only.
4. It can be a dev-dependency only, if we replace the staging folder with `std` code. The tests need it. We can do this change in this PR if you want it.

**`rustix`** (Linux and macOS) and **`windows-sys`** (Windows)
1. `rename_new` publishes the staging folder with a rename that does not replace an existing destination (`renameat` with `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, `MoveFileW`). This prevents an overwrite of a job that another process made after the existence check.
2. No. `std::fs::rename` replaces an empty destination folder on Unix. `std` has no rename without replace. `std::fs::hard_link` and `File::create_new` work on files only, not on folders.
3. No. I found no crate in the workspace that gives a rename without replace.
4. They are behind a `cfg` for each platform now: `rustix` only on Linux and Apple, `windows-sys` only on Windows. They cannot be dev-dependencies, because the export uses them.

Please tell us if `tempfile` must change to a dev-dependency. The two platform crates have no `std` replacement.
Back to draft. I merge main into this branch now. The merge changes the head, so the PR must be a draft while I push and gate it.

I merged main `09ad779ee` into this branch. The new head is `e99d91acc`.

`cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 3219 --reviewed d982d452b` gives NEW CODE:

- `e99d91acc`: one fix, so that main's test `the_post_page_without_setups_has_no_extra_separator` passes.

Please review `git diff d982d452b..e99d91acc`. The PR body has the details and the gate results for this head.

After the merge, this PR does not change `crates/post/Cargo.toml`. `tempfile`, `rustix` and `windows-sys` are on main since #2951 (see my earlier reply on the four questions). This PR adds no dependency.

Request to the maintainer: please remove the `needs-maintainer` label, if you agree that the dependency question is closed. Please also remove `conflicts`: the branch now merges cleanly with main.

I mark this PR ready now.

Correction to my last comment: the branch does not merge cleanly now. Main moved to 6167d30af (#3731) after my check, and #3731 changed the generated file docs/agents/mcp-tools.md. This PR goes back to draft. I will merge main, generate the file again with camcraft-cli mcp reference, run the MCP tests, push and flag the PR ready again. Please ignore my request to remove conflicts until then.

I merged main 6167d30af into this branch. The new head is d12d6e331. GitHub now reports the PR as mergeable (clean).

The only conflict was the generated file docs/agents/mcp-tools.md. I generated it again with camcraft-cli mcp reference. Against main, it adds only the two tools of this PR. The tests mcp_doc_drift, mcp_dxf and the app lib passed on this head, and Clippy on camcraft-app gave no warnings. The PR body has the readings.

Please review git diff d982d452b..d12d6e331 (NEW CODE: two merges of main and one fix commit). My request to remove needs-maintainer and conflicts is valid again.

I mark this PR ready now.
